_doc: Fixtures still routed OUT of the in-process differential oracle because their spend needs a cryptographic witness that the plain oracle cannot synthesise from bare args. Post-mortem remediation #1 gave the oracle REAL secp256k1: every stateless/stateful ECDSA-checkSig / checkMultiSig fixture that could be given a real signature was MOVED to conformance/witnesses/real-crypto/ (executed for real on @bsv/sdk Spend) and removed from this list. What REMAINS here is genuinely out of reach for the current TS real-crypto harness. The free-text `reason` is for humans; the machine-checked truth of each entry's claim lives in its `coveredBy` field (see coverage-claims.test.ts) — membership in this list is NOT itself treated as coverage. See conformance/witnesses/README.md.

exempt.reason: zero-mutable-field StatefulSmartContract (issue #44): RunarContract.prepareCall derives isStateful from stateFields.length>0, which is false here, so it exposes the auto-injected SigHashPreimage as a REQUIRED user arg and the standard call([null]) continuation path does not apply — the tx-context preimage cannot be supplied via the SDK call() harness. FOLLOW-UP: drive it via a hand-built preimage in the TS harness.

coveredBy.note: real deploy + terminal claim() spend on a live regtest node (accept-only; gated behind `cargo test --features regtest`); proves the parentClass sighash-trim fix, not a full accept/reject differential.

exempt.reason: BLAKE3 hash-preimage (blake3Compress/blake3Hash) — not a secp256k1 signature

coveredBy.note: script_execution_test.go also has func TestBlake3Hash_* real-execution tests; both run inline blake3Compress/blake3Hash contracts through the real Go BSV SDK Spend, not the literal 'blake3' fixture file.

exempt.reason: secp256k1 EC ops (ecAdd/ecMulGen/ecNegate) — EC point witness, not a checkSig

stateless SmartContract mixing checkSig + checkPreimage + extractOutputHash — needs a hand-built SigHashPreimage arg bound to a specific expected output; the stateless single-input signed harness cannot synthesise it. FOLLOW-UP candidate for the TS real-crypto harness.

coveredBy.note: real deploy + spend on a live regtest node: TestCovenantVault_ValidSpend (accept) and TestCovenantVault_WrongOutput_Rejected (reject) — both against examples/ts/covenant-vault/CovenantVault.runar.ts, the exact .runar.ts source this fixture resolves to.

exempt.reason: hash256 preimage verification — hash-preimage witness, not a checkSig. NOTE: hash256 is a base builtin (no dedicated codegen module; see packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/04-anf-lower.ts), unlike the special-cased sha256Compress/sha256Finalize family, so this exemption's justification is weaker than the others in this file — it likely COULD be witnessed by the plain oracle (pick any bytes, compute hash256 locally, no real signature needed) but nobody has written that spec yet.

coveredBy.note: byte-golden only (expected-script.hex); no dedicated per-family codegen module exists for hash256 since it is a base builtin, not a special-cased primitive like sha256Compress/Finalize.

exempt.reason: SLH-DSA-SHA2-128f verification — huge PQ witness. UPGRADED from byte-golden-only: conformance/script_execution_test.go now compiles and EXECUTES this exact fixture with a real, independently cross-checked-valid signature (packages/runar-go's native impl, byte-identical to the TS reference impl) on the go-sdk interpreter, and the compiled script ACCEPTS it (and REJECTS a tampered / wrong-message signature). The pre-existing SLH-DSA codegen miscompile that made it reject a genuinely valid signature (emitSLHHmsg multi-block CAT order) is now FIXED byte-identically across all 7 tiers (audit #2).
